Projects.intro: Here are some of my latest works, some are unfinished side projects, others are freelance client projects. Every project is coded solo and lives somewhere on my GitHub.
Projects.beatriceDesc: Beatrice generates and publishes SEO articles for Next.js, WordPress, or any stack that can consume an API. You plug your project in and content ships automatically.
Projects.beatriceWorkDone:
Beatrice is a Next.js product I built: an SEO content engine with an API, a dashboard, and generated articles (topics, long-form copy, metadata, FAQs, WebP images, internal links).

Technically it covers the full article lifecycle: paginated lists, editing, publishing, compressed images, alt text. The goal is close to a small headless CMS, but focused on SEO and automation.

Integrations described on the site (Next.js, WordPress, other stacks) use straightforward endpoints to pull content in production.
Projects.beatriceMission: Automate SEO blogging so the product team does not live in a spreadsheet.
Projects.optionZeroDesc: Website for Option Zéro, the free app that helps people regain control over alcohol use (CaPASSCité association, aligned with French public health guidance). Institutional pages, blog, donations, links to the stores.
Projects.optionZeroWorkDone:
The public site option-zero.fr promotes the Option Zéro app: what it does, the mission, blog posts, campaigns such as “Tournée minérale”, donations, FAQ, testimonials, and download links to the stores.

I worked on Next.js development and layout, responsive polish, and SEO/SEA support so people searching for help actually find the right pages.

It is a public health project: tone and information architecture matter as much as performance.
Projects.optionZeroMission: Give a clear, trustworthy web base for a free harm-reduction service.
Projects.lolTrackerDesc: Tool for Flex 5 teams in League of Legends: stats, detailed ratings (including an MVP score), and match history so you see who really improves.
Projects.lolTrackerWorkDone:
LoL Tracker answers “how did we play tonight?” with numbers. You sign up, add five summoner names, and games are tracked automatically.

Built with Next.js, DaisyUI, and Clerk for auth. You get per-player stats, team history, and an MVP score that goes beyond KDA (vision, gold per minute, kill participation, as explained on the site).

Riot’s API quotas are tight, so caching and batched calls keep things smooth without hammering their servers.
Projects.lolTrackerMission: Help a Flex 5 squad see clearly who contributes what, game after game.
Projects.captimedDesc: Mobile app for medical interns: time tracking, PHQ-9 mood check-in, resources and support. Listed on captimed.fr and the app stores.
Projects.captimedWorkDone:
CapTimed targets interns who stack shifts and still need a paper trail for hours and headspace. React Native on the client, Express on the server, NativeWind for UI, Zustand for state.

The marketing site highlights time tracking, the PHQ-9 questionnaire, access to support, and articles about rights and burnout. The goal is a practical tool in a field where workload is often understated.
Projects.captimedMission: Give interns one simple place to log time and look after themselves.
Projects.nekjeuDesc: Real-time web game: two players hear the same Nekfeu track; the first to guess the album scores points.
Projects.nekjeuWorkDone:
Nekjeu runs on a Laravel backend (audio files, game logic) and Vue.js in the browser, with Socket.io to keep both players on the same round.

The hard part is audio sync: timestamps, latency, recovering from drift. Matchmaking pairs two players for back-to-back rounds.
Projects.nekjeuMission: Offer a fun duel between fans without pretending to replace Spotify.
Projects.bananegamesDesc: Free edutainment hub: today Etymot (words) and GeoExplorer (geography), with a Laravel site for pages and news.
Projects.bananegamesWorkDone:
Banane Games is the hub that showcases the games and publishes news. The Laravel back office manages site content and articles.

Each game is its own Vue.js web app: Etymot for French, GeoExplorer for geography, with a light tone aimed at younger learners.
Projects.bananegamesMission: Ship free games that still help at school.
Projects.g2Desc: Small G2 Esports tool: upload a photo, PhotoRoom cuts the subject out, you drop it on a “detonate” style frame ready to share.
Projects.g2WorkDone:
Client Laravel project around the PhotoRoom API: upload, masking, composition with G2 visuals, export for social.

Most of the work was keeping response times acceptable with heavy images and making the image pipeline reliable end to end.
Projects.g2Mission: Give fans a fast way to post on-brand visuals.
Projects.cdcDesc: Small showcase site around hunting dogs and the web services two enthusiasts offer.
Projects.cdcWorkDone: Landing site to explain the project, list services, and make contact easy. Simple layout, mobile first, trust blocks so visitors quickly understand who is behind it.
Projects.cdcMission: Keep the story clear without overbuilding the page.
Projects.bordersDesc: Web configurator for Summoner Frame: preview League of Legends frames (colors, finishes) before ordering instead of guessing from a PDF.
Projects.bordersWorkDone:
Borders.gg is a Next.js app (DaisyUI, Aceternity-style components) wired to the LoL frame catalog. You tweak the config, see the preview update, and land on the right product in the shop.

The main challenge was UX: many variants, low friction, preview that tracks choices in real time.
Projects.bordersMission: Make ordering a custom frame as readable as a car configurator.
Projects.qoffeeDesc: Training lab: pull content from a WordPress blog and render it in a Next.js 14 app (App Router).
Projects.qoffeeWorkDone: Qoffee is a thread for my classes: consume WordPress content, then wire it into Next 14 with the new routing model. Students practice fetch, rendering, and sane project structure instead of one giant component.
Projects.qoffeeMission: Bridge a classic CMS and a modern React stack.
Projects.coursWorkDone:
perso-forma.vercel.app sells a bootcamp prep pack: landing that explains the method (videos, Figma files, corrections, Discord), FAQ, testimonials, checkout for the €49 offer.

Next.js, DaisyUI, Stripe for payments. It is the product side of my teaching work, not just a blog.
Projects.coursMission: Ship a serious exercise path before students jump into bootcamp.
Projects.fuchsWorkDone: Small Next.js / DaisyUI game hooked to the client image set. Rounds are fast (the site mentions a one-minute timer), so players rely on instinct more than theory.
Projects.fuchsMission: Make the “AI or not?” question feel like a game.
Projects.kraiWorkDone: KRAI was a personal Laravel playground: Blade views, Bootstrap layout, parallax sections to add depth without reaching for a heavy JS framework.
Projects.kraiMission: Practice Laravel while keeping the page pleasant to scroll.
Projects.legendsFusionWorkDone:
Legends’ Fusion follows the on-site rules: five rounds in a row, each time a random champion and you pick one spell (Q, W, E, R, or passive) without knowing the next champion, so the kit is partly guesswork.

Next.js on the front, short replayable sessions, credit in the footer. Fun and spell knowledge matter more than competitive balance.
Projects.legendsFusionMission: Test absurd synergies between League of Legends champions.
Projects.mvpWorkDone:
MVP Tracker starts from a simple fact: OP.GG does not expose a full public API for everything you might want to chart. Puppeteer fetches pages, SQLite stores history so we do not hammer the site, Chart.js draws the trends.

When OP.GG changes markup, selectors need updates. The project taught me responsible scraping (cache, frequency) plus basic visualization.
Projects.mvpMission: Turn opaque web pages into charts you can actually read.
Projects.pokedexWorkDone: The Pokédex is a class exercise around fetch, the DOM, and a rich REST API (types, sprites, pagination), all in vanilla JS on purpose so students see what a framework will later abstract away.
Projects.pokedexMission: Teach API integration with a universe everyone already knows.
Projects.ronronnerieWorkDone: Client site on WordPress and Elementor for a cat café in central Nice: photos, practical info, booking flow depending on what they needed to highlight. Most of the effort was layout, copy, and a clean mobile experience for tourists searching on the go.
Projects.ronronnerieMission: Make the venue easy to find online as a real Nice cat café.
Projects.supdecoursWorkDone:
SupDeCours is Laravel with TinyMCE for rich text, teacher and student roles, and Bootstrap so CSS does not eat the whole schedule.

Goal is practical: publish a course, attach files, let students grab everything from one place.
Projects.supdecoursMission: Centralize class material without juggling five tools.
Projects.quizbrainWorkDone: QuizBrain mixes the App Router, server rendering, and a question web service so students see how a quiz app is structured (dynamic routes, minimal client state).
Projects.quizbrainMission: Show Next.js on a case close to what they will see at work.
Projects.trouveMotWorkDone:
trouve-mot.fr documents the API live: random draws, filters by letter, category, length, word of the day / week / month. The homepage advertises 3,575+ words across 27 categories.

Classic Laravel with MySQL behind it. Queries are tuned where it matters without over-engineering the stack.
Projects.trouveMotMission: Offer a free word API for games and generators.
Projects.monacotraductionWorkDone:
WordPress build with Elementor and Polylang for Monaco Traduction: written translation, interpreting, training, and sector pages (legal, luxury, yachting, and more).

Each language keeps its own pages, contact and quote forms follow, and SEO is handled per locale for a Monaco-based agency.
Projects.monacotraductionMission: Give a serious agency a site that matches its positioning.
Projects.wabiSabiSuitesWorkDone:
Wabi Sabi Suites runs on WordPress and Elementor. The site has a lot going on: apartments by city, the hybrid Le Lorrain hotel in Nice, the concept page, gallery, bookings. My focus was to structure that so visitors get it quickly and local SEO doesn’t fall apart.

What I actually did on the theme and in Elementor:

  • Added and laid out pages for cities, accommodations, and the hotel side vs. the apartment side
  • Local SEO work: titles, copy, internal links so Nice, Cannes, and Villefranche-sur-Mer are covered sensibly, without messy duplication
  • Bug fixes (layouts breaking, blocks acting weird)
  • Tweaks for smaller screens, since a lot of traffic is mobile

The point is you can tell apart a self-catering stay from the furnished hotel experience, and the site stays dependable day to day.

I kept everything on their WordPress and Elementor setup so they can keep updating without reinventing the wheel.
Projects.wabiSabiSuitesMission: Make the offer clear on the site and shore up local search around Nice, Cannes, and Villefranche-sur-Mer.
